claim: The safety net (deploy_image auto-rollback) reverts images, but the 17 migrations are forward-only, so after the first apply the rollback unit is no longer the deploy; and nothing has ever run these images or SQL outside PGlite (no dev fleet, db-guard probes "only run on PGlite"). Shipping 277 commits, 700 files and 17 migrations in one window with the DB in an unknown restricted state removes the ability to attribute a failure to a cause, so the range should be split into independently verifiable slices (migration+image pairs per product) rather than gated as one go.

A reader cannot tell what was actually verified: the shipping list handed to the council is a draft at dbc49fa1b (161 commits, 15 migrations), while the subject is 681430ac5 (277 commits, 17 migrations). The "all pending / no checksum drift" check covers neither 076 nor 118, nor the roughly 116 commits added after dbc49fa1b. The "re-cut" list the brief calls authoritative was not provided, so the owner's typed go could quote a plan that does not match the shipped sha.

The rollback story is image-only: deploy_image auto-rollback never reverts a migration, and 075_retire_one_chat.sql (lines 20-44) irreversibly deletes the one-chat catalogue rows, control rows and the stored social_wiring_api_token. If the agents image is rolled back after 075, the old ensure_default_agents re-seeds one-chat while the bridge credential is gone, leaving a half-working state, and the plan names no per-step rollback or a pre-075 data snapshot. 072 also rewrites the live publish_agent_version gate (072:212-351), so the shipping list must state the old image still works against the new function before the migrations run.

The six inactive products that import the seed WhatsApp integration with no declared policy are a known fail-closed trap on their next rebuild. The seed could ship a derived, fleet-wide default declaration, or a keeper that fails any importer lacking a policy, so this is fixed once instead of per product at wake-up. The same applies to the migration dry-run that b5 ran by hand: wrapping it as a reusable pre-ship tool would re-verify 076 and 118, which were never checked.

The first precondition for any prod step is knowing whether the database can be written and read at all, yet the egress restriction extent is deliberately unknown and the "continue, im aware" acknowledgment does not establish that migrations or the new images' startup reads will succeed. A migration run that dies partway on a restricted project (075 deletes catalogue rows and a stored credential, 338 and others are multi-statement) leaves a half-applied schema with images pinned to the old or new side, so a verified-unrestricted read/write probe by the owner must be an explicit gate before the first apply, not a known open condition.

The brief names no rollback for the irreversible steps, and "auto-rollback" covers only the image. Migration 075 hard-DELETEs the one-chat catalog and agent rows and the stored SW api token (075_retire_one_chat.sql:20-44), and 073/072 drop constraints and a function signature. None of this is reversible by deploy_image, and there is no stated backup or restore point before the apply.

Migration 075 (products/agents/backend/migrations/075_retire_one_chat.sql:20-44) irreversibly DELETEs catalogue rows, agent control rows and the stored social_wiring_api_token with no backup or snapshot step in the shipping list, and its correctness depends on a cross-product ordering (agents image, then 075, then SW image, then token revoke) that breaks if the night ends mid-sequence. The list should require a pre-apply dump of those three tables and state the resting state if the sequence stops after 075 but before the SW image or revoke.

The shipping list is stale and its own re-cut is pending: it is cut at dbc49fa1b with 15 migrations, while the final sha is 681430ac5 with 17, and the owner's typed go must quote the deploy plan. The list also leaves the post-step order ambiguous (token revoke, drop SOCIAL_WIRING_API_TOKEN, db-guard probes after 338, verify_db_guards core and agents after each apply) with no end-of-night checklist saying what is left half-done. Require a single re-cut list at 681430ac5 with a per-step verify command and a stop-safe state before any go is typed.

The shipping list is stale against the range: it was cut at dbc49fa1b (161 commits, 15 migrations verified pending) while the subject is 681430ac5 (277 commits), and 076 and 118 plus the seed line-policy are unverified against the prod ledger. A go typed against a list that does not name the final sha and ledger state asks the owner to consent to something not yet described.

The window is too large for one night: 700 files across 5 images, 17 migrations, a token revoke and 3 owner-only steps, with no dev fleet and prod as the first run of every image. The smallest safe alternative is obvious from the dependency list but not offered. Ship seed/core/monica-safe pieces first, and hold the agents image + 075 + SW image chain and the vitrine/lead-backfill steps for a second window.

17 migrations across three products in one night against a Supabase project in an unknown exceed_egress_quota restriction can fail midway (e.g. agents 072-074 applied, 075 not), and the ledger state for 076 and 118 was never checked. Make the go conditional on a successful read-only migrate_product dry-run at the final sha 681430ac5 immediately before the first apply, with a stated stop point after each product. The smallest safe alternative is core (115-118) and agents (072-076) tonight, and SW 331-338 plus its owner-only post-steps on a later day, since the image-before-075-then-SW order leaves the SW bridge calling a retired endpoint in the gap.

The Supabase egress restriction is treated as "known, owner aware" with no go/no-go criterion, though the shipping list itself calls it a ship blocker until understood. Migrations, db-guard probes, smoke tests and rollback health checks all depend on the DB, so a half-applied 17-migration sequence under a throttled project could leave the fleet unobservable. A cheap read-only check should be an explicit precondition.

The shipment is framed as all-or-nothing (277 commits, 17 migrations), but a split is available: ship the seed, monica and additive migrations tonight, and hold the destructive and owner-dependent parts for a second window. Migration 075 DELETEs the one-chat agent rows and the stored SW token (075_retire_one_chat.sql:20-44), the migrations have no down path, and the shipping list has no snapshot or restore step for those rows. Supabase is egress-restricted, which is the very condition that could fail an apply midway.

Migration 338 is forward-only and its own header admits the previous social-wiring image's `nao_realizada` writes now violate the new visitas CHECK, and it drops/recreates vw_imovel_visita_contagem without the `nao_realizadas` column. So deploy_image's auto-rollback (image only) after 338 returns prod to an image that cannot write visits, and the shipping list never orders 338 versus the SW image swap. Name the order (SW image and 338 as one step, with the schema-incompatible window stated) and say there is no rollback past 338 except a forward fix.

Agents 075 deletes `one-chat` rows in agents.agents and only falls back to archiving on foreign_key_violation. But 037, 049 and 050 declare FKs to agents.agents ON DELETE CASCADE (and 048/042/057 SET NULL), so for those tables the delete succeeds silently and destroys child rows or nulls the audit linkage instead of archiving. The "owns history → archive" promise is only true for the NO ACTION FKs; count the cascade-child rows for key='one-chat' in prod before applying.

The seed line policy (D2b) fails closed and rides every rebuilt image, and the six inactive products declare no policy, so this range plants a latent refusal that any later rebuild of them triggers. Tonight's safety rests on a manually verified `"*"` wildcard in the social-wiring compose, tagged NOC-REMEDIATE[sw-waha-host-declaration], which permits send on every SW line rather than a declared one. Verify the policy against the live VPS compose (not the repo) before the swap, and record the wildcard as a time-boxed exception with an owner.

The brief treats a Supabase project restricted for exceed_egress_quota as "known, not a blocker", yet its extent is unprobed and the prod ledger for 076 and 118 is unverified, while 17 migrations, 4 image swaps and a consent step the brief itself calls forgeable are planned into one window. A restriction that bites mid-run leaves forward-only migrations applied against old images, and auto-rollback does not undo schema. The smallest safe alternative is to ship nothing until a ledger read succeeds and the owner confirms the cap, then split: seed/line-policy images plus core 115-118 first, agents 072-076 and SW 331-338 in a later window.

The CPF/RG import flag `importar_identidade` (337) can be switched on by any org admin of any org through PUT /api/leads/vista-clientes/config (vista_clientes.py:112-119). The contract (ad-lead-intake-CONTRACT.md:253-254) says it stays OFF until a legal read is recorded, so that gate is enforced by convention only. Before go-live, either lock the switch to platform-admin, or require the legal read (OAB lawyer + encarregado) to be recorded and checked before CPF/RG matching and import are enabled for any org.

SW 337 + vista_clientes_sync.py:64-80 make the first persisting consumer of Vista clientes (birth date, civil status, profession, full address), which LGPD-WARNINGS.md:18-19 says must pass the data-category intake first, yet the range adds no LGPD-WARNINGS/ROPA entry and the basis in ad-lead-intake-CONTRACT.md:251-254 is legitimate interest (LGPD art 7 IX and art 10) with no written balancing test (LIA). The code may ship because the sync is manual, admin-only and dry-run by default. Before prod, no confirm=True sync may run for any org until the controller (the org) has recorded the LIA and instructed the enrichment (LGPD art 39), and the encarregado has reviewed it.

SW 334/335 add broker personal data to lead_corretores (email, celular, creci, data_saida) and state "never deleted" (334:9), so contact data of former brokers has no end-of-purpose deletion (LGPD arts 15 I and 16). imovel_corretores (331) also stores name, email and phone of partner brokers from other agencies, and 334:7 and 334:34 commit a named broker into git. Recommend a retention rule keyed on data_saida and removing the name from the comment.

Profession and address that the 337 sync fills from Vista (origem 'vista', possibly years old) reach the contract generator's party qualification without any provenance flag (contrato_gerador/carregador.py:428,434). This bears on the LGPD data-quality principle (art 6 V), and the lawyer's per-version review cannot see that these values were never confirmed. Recommend marking Vista-origin qualification fields "a confirmar" in the generator.

The SW api_token 8565469e is revoked only as a trailing post-step, yet the new agents image no longer reads it (075_retire_one_chat.sql:44 deletes the stored copy; no SOCIAL_WIRING_API_TOKEN under products/agents/backend/app at 681430ac5). The old SW image is still honoured, and it is also deploy_image's rollback target; it still accepts the scope social-wiring:one-chat:toggle (agents_bridge_router.py:80-81 at 8293844b5), which writes the org's WhatsApp auto-reply. Revoke the token, and drop it from the agents env, as soon as the agents image is healthy and before the SW swap, so a night that ends mid-deploy leaves no live orphaned write credential.

The owner's live typed consent is the only control on tonight's prod writes (prod_consent is forgeable, ce8552e6c), yet the plan it quotes still scopes the range to dev dbc49fa1b with 161 commits (shipping-list-draft.md:3-4), while the real range ends at 681430ac5 with 277 commits. The 116 commits and 197 files after dbc49fa1b include the D2b seed line policy that goes into every image, the stage-2 notify_owner, the pre-push change, and migrations 076 and 118. The go only counts if the owner types it live in b5's session naming 681430ac5 and all 17 migration filenames in their order; a go on the dbc49fa1b plan does not cover what ships.

decision: Ship SPLIT; no prod step before preconditions 1-3 pass. Window 1 (tonight if they pass): core 115-118 → core image → verify_db_guards core; then the monica image. Window 2 (owner-dated): agents 072-074 → agents image → 075, 076 → verify_db_guards agents → revoke token 8565469e and drop SOCIAL_WIRING_API_TOKEN; then the social-wiring image with 331-338 as one step → 338 db-guard probes; owner-only post-steps last. Each slice is one blessed sha with its own live typed go and a stop-safe state.
biggest_risk: The rollback net covers images only, while migrations are forward-only. 073 drops the 8-arg publish_agent_version (the old agents image can't publish), the 338 CHECK breaks the old SW image's nao_realizada writes, and 075 hard-deletes rows. A partial run on a restricted Supabase project leaves schema and images mismatched with only a fix forward.
first_step: In b5's session, re-cut the shipping list at 681430ac5, then run a read-only migrate_product dry-run at sha=681430ac5 for core, agents and social-wiring (this is also the Supabase reachability probe). Gates: pre-push kept; merge queue kept; predeploy_check kept (at 681430ac5); deploy_image auto-rollback kept (the plan states it is images-only); prod_consent changed (a live typed go per slice naming the sha and that slice's migration filenames); migration ledger kept (read at the final sha, must cover 076 and 118).

note: Tech-lead ratifies the split plan as is. Precondition 6 (the Vista PUT /config gate) will be closed by a code fix, locking it to platform-admin per contract line 253 before window 2, rather than by owner risk acceptance. Deferred H/P/Q route to the named backlogs.

Partial overrule of precondition 1 (owner challenge, 2026-11-10: "why? It doesnt block you"). Verified in code: migrate_product and verify_db_guards use the direct DB connection, and b5's dry-run at 681430ac5 succeeded on it; deploy_image judges /api/health, whose default liveness is always-200 and does not call Supabase. The egress restriction only hits the API path (PostgREST/catalog), which prod apps are already affected by whether or not we deploy. Amended precondition 1: the dry-run at the final sha must succeed on the direct DB (done by b5); an egress lift is NOT required. Post-deploy judgement relies on health + verify_db_guards, not an API smoke. Rest of the verdict unchanged.
